chunks: Remember, when your Lord said to the angels: "I have to place a trustee on the earth," they said: "Will You place one there who would create disorder and shed blood, while we intone Your litanies and sanctify Your name?" And God said: "I know what you do not know."

key_terms.خَلِيفَةً: Vicegerent or trustee, referring to Adam's role as God's representative on Earth
key_terms.نُسَبِّحُ: We glorify (referring to the angels' worship)

ai.seo_question: Why did the angels ask God if He would place someone on Earth who would shed blood?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the concept of *Khilafah* not merely as physical stewardship but as a spiritual and intellectual vicegerency, highlighting Adam's unique capacity for divine knowledge (*Ilm*) that surpassed the angels' literal understanding. The angels' query reflects their limited perspective on divine wisdom, while God's response underscores the superiority of human potential to embody both knowledge and free will. This foundational event sets the stage for the prophetic and imamate lineage, where the Imam serves as the perfect representative of God's knowledge on Earth.
